Four folding stands for the quartet. Prototype must fit inside the old bus locker, maximum folded length 62 cm.
Start finish tests for museum mandolin on offcuts. Amber wash over isolation layer; record the mix so the touch-up can later be removed.
Close view under mandolin top: one loose brace stops just before the crack. Pencil marks show where the two cleats may sit.
stand hinge squeaks / drill jig hole wandering / try hand reamer
Finish card: mix amber 3, clear 7. Under cool light it looks too orange next to the mandolin's worn edge.
Curator approved two small cleats on the mandolin split, keeping the stamped date visible. Photograph the stamp before installation.
62? lid won't shut
Quartet bus locker was measured with the lid open. Correct folded-stand limit to 58 cm, replacing the earlier 62; shorten the lower rail drawing.
Mandolin repair test: the amber 3/clear 7 sample obscures grain under exhibition lighting. Retire that recipe; the new card is amber 1/clear 9 over the same isolation layer.
Cleats glued and clamp pressure released. Mandolin seam stays shut with no string load; do not add tension just to prove a display repair.
Finish notebook page for the mandolin: one-to-nine mix stays translucent after drying. Removal test lifts it without disturbing the isolation coat.
Quartet stand prototype folds to 57.5 cm now. Bass player tried opening it one-handed; add a thumb notch in the latch.

Joint review with curator: mandolin seam is stable with two cleats; coat only the pale exposed line using the one-to-nine amber trial. Add both the cleat positions and finish-removal method to the conservation record. We looked at the top first under the bench lamp and then under the warmer exhibition lamp. The repaired line is more noticeable under the bench lamp, but the curator prefers that to covering the surrounding original surface. Leave the little dark scratch beside the treble foot alone; it appears in the oldest photograph and is not part of this damage. Before applying colour, photograph the closed seam with a scale and mark the two cleats on a separate underside sketch. Attach the approved offcut sample number and isolation-coat notes so a future conservator can distinguish our touch-up from the original finish.
Under magnification the mandolin cleats have no squeezed-out glue near the stamp. Conservation photo accepted.
Tin labelled 'clear' has no mixing date. Don't use until identified.
Quartet rails cut as a set of four. One knot at the hinge line: remake that rail before assembling the remaining stands.
Dry mandolin touch-up viewed from normal gallery distance. Curator says the pale line no longer distracts; store the approved sample card with recipe.
Museum signed off the mandolin's stable display condition. Foam support must carry the neck; repaired top should bear no mounting weight.
All four quartet stands fit the locker and open with the new thumb notch. Write the hinge oiling note on their care sheet.

items.text: Slate Ridge Saturday: bus to Mill Gate, climb by the eastern path, camp at the old quarry. Seven kilometres carrying packs.
Miso sitter: Ana can do Saturday dinner but needs the key before Friday. Cat food is in the red cupboard.
Tent test in shower: slow drip along the foot-end seam. Mark the wet spot with tape; buy seam sealer.
Ridge food for three: oats twice, lentil packets Saturday night, wraps for lunches. Ben cannot eat sesame.
Friday client report handoff: Jules needs the draft charts by Thursday noon to cover my leave.
Map enlargement shows the quarry is inside the no-camping zone. Revise Slate Ridge overnight stop to Juniper Field; add two kilometres to Saturday.
Tent foot seam cleaned and sealed. Cure flat indoors for a full day before repeating the water test.
Voice memo lost the start: 'three, red one, before Friday'.
Juniper Field has a tap by the gate, but the notice says seasonal. Phone the caretaker before deciding how much water to carry on the ridge.
Ana has the key and Miso's feeding card. She asked me to leave a light on a timer.
Client report charts exported. Jules spotted a missing legend on revenue; fix it before sending the Thursday handoff.

Call with caretaker: Juniper Field tap shut this weekend. Move the route's lunch stop to Mill Spring for a refill, and pack an extra two-litre bladder plus a no-boil dinner so our water plan still works.
Second tent shower test: the foot seam stays dry after ten minutes. Repack only when the fly has dried.
Rename our 'Slate Ridge weekend' route sheet to 'Juniper loop'. It's still the same bus, walkers and revised Juniper Field camp; easier to distinguish from last year's ridge plan.
Lentil packet labels have sesame oil. Replace all three with the chickpea pouches; Ben checked those ingredients.
Miso's sitter backup is Omar if Ana's late shift runs over. Both have the same feeding card; don't double the evening meal.
Jules received the client report with revenue legend restored. Leave note says he owns any Friday edits.
Juniper loop GPX now includes Mill Spring and the extra distance. Download it before leaving mobile coverage.
Green bag by the door. Check whether it has the small one.
Ridge meals packed: sesame-free chickpeas, wraps, oats, extra bladder. Put Ben's marked pouch at the top for the spring lunch stop.

Breakfast urn trial holds coffee above our service target for ninety minutes. Preheat with hot water, empty, then fill just before leaving for the archive.
A clear one, not fourteen. check supplier.
Bin contract name on quote is 'Extra uplift'. Rename our admin folder to 'Food bin schedule'; still the same twice-weekly food-waste proposal.

Pastry supply changed for Friday: bakery replaces pear twists with apple pockets. Order ten pockets instead of fourteen twists, and replace the counter allergen card with the supplier's wheat/milk/almond declaration before displaying them.
Window installer measured west pane twice: 132 by 186 cm inside the seals. Approved clear film sample after viewing at three o'clock.
Archive host revised headcount to twenty-four. Coffee delivery stays 08:15; reduce brewed volume and send the revised catering total.
Apple pocket allergen card proof: wheat, milk, almond in bold, product name above. Keep pear-twist card in the retired folder so it isn't put back accidentally.
Food bin schedule accepted: Tuesday and Friday collections, smaller bin, month-to-month. First Tuesday pickup starts next week.
Friday pastry close: ten apple pockets in, eight sold, two donated; zero discarded. Keep Monday order at ten pending another day's sales.
On the counter, by the old sheet. Ask Mina.
West window film installed with a small bubble at the top. Installer says inspect after three days; screen is readable this afternoon.
Archive meeting coffee delivered 08:10 for twenty-four. Urn returned empty and clean; final invoice matches revised headcount.
Counter check: apple pocket sign matches the current bakery ingredient declaration. No pear-twist labels left among today's trays.

items.text: Bay Museum requests the celestial globe for Navigating at Night, four months from June. Loan committee needs their case specification and light-level plan before approval.
Returning mask from Ash Gallery due next Wednesday. Compare carved edge with the outgoing condition photos before signing receipt.
Globe crate sketch: suspended inner cradle, no pressure on meridian ring. Outside width estimate 82 cm including foam and handles.
Please check the ring before signing. Message forwarded without attachment or sender context.
Paper archive humidity climbs whenever the supply fan stops. Technician wants a week of readings from the independent logger.
Choir altos: pencilled breath after 'water', not before it. Make six copies of the marked score for Monday rehearsal.
Bay sent the globe case drawing with a supported brass base and controlled lights. Committee approved the loan subject to the signed indemnity schedule.
Crate maker measured globe on its base: outside width must be 91 cm, replacing the 82 cm sketch. Larger handles included in the new figure; check the loading-door opening.
Ash mask return condition sheet: old chip beside left eye unchanged, but new scrape on the underside of the stand. Photograph before moving it off the unpacking table.
Courier route sheet has globe outward collection and Ash mask return on the same vehicle. Mask paperwork stays with receiving registrar; globe crate can load only after the return is unloaded.
Archive logger shows peaks at fan stoppages, not when the door opens. Service company bringing a replacement relay on Thursday.

Globe dispatch review with Bay: approve the loan schedule with the revised packed dimensions, and attach the signed case/light conditions to the agreement. Transport team must use a liftgate van because the completed 91 cm crate cannot go through the smaller side door. The host registrar will receive the sealed crate at the loading bay and send the seal photograph before their crew opens it. Committee approval alone is not our dispatch release; release comes after the crate maker confirms the cradle holds the base without touching the meridian ring. Pack a copy of the agreed handling diagram in the outer document pocket so nobody needs to break the seal to find it. Bay's registrar has checked the revised loan schedule and will return the signature page after their facilities team confirms the liftgate arrival slot.
Choir director changed the alto breath: take it before 'water' after all, together with tenors. Mark the correction on all six rehearsal copies.
Ash Gallery agrees the mask stand scrape is new. Registrar will retain the comparison photos and record the accepted repair contribution against this return.
Globe cradle test filmed with dummy load: base stays level through the ramp angle, meridian ring area remains clear. Crate maker signed release sheet.
Bay globe agreement signed by both registrars. Loan dates remain June through September; exhibition credit line now includes the donor family.
New archive relay fitted. Supply fan ran overnight and the paper-room logger stayed inside the set band; keep logging through Monday.
Globe van collected at the agreed bay. Crate seal and liftgate loading photographed; send tracking update to Bay registrar.
Mask return reconciled: receiving signature, scrape photographs and contribution agreement all filed. Move object back to its assigned store shelf.
Monday choir pack ready, six alto scores with the revised breath mark. Keep one crossed-out original so I remember which instruction changed.

items.text: Loose slip from tote: 'third one too weak; move it' with a smudged arrow.
Embroidered hanging survey: fading strongest along top third, two weak stitches at lower sleeve. Compare against last year's colour target photographs.
Home fence blew over at the corner. Save the undamaged gate; price three replacement panels and two posts.
Hanging tour draft: Bell House in March, Estuary Rooms in April, Hill Centre in May. Each venue wants a full calendar month.
Textile courier coverage: Sal available March only; Mina can do April and May if dates avoid her course. Need someone trained to supervise unrolling.
Survey under raking light shows lower sleeve stitches hold at rest but pull when hanging vertically. Recommend a sloped support board instead of free hanging.
Bell House can build the sloped support. Their conservator asks us to send the exact board angle with the condition report.
Tour revision: Hill Centre cannot control daylight, so remove its May slot. Bell House remains March; Estuary Rooms gets April plus the first week of May.
Mina's course moved to 3 May. She can take the hanging to Estuary in April but cannot supervise its return on 7 May; seek return cover.
'Mina / 7 / angle?' heard over station announcement.
Fence supplier quote is for four panels by mistake. We need three; gate stays. Revised dimensions marked on corner sketch.
Tour renamed from 'Three rooms' to 'Stitched journeys' after dropping Hill Centre. Keep existing Bell House and Estuary agreements under the new project heading.
Textile support trial passed at 20 degrees from vertical. Record the lower sleeve's weak stitches on the courier condition diagram so any change during unpacking can be compared to today's survey.

Stitched journeys return plan: shorten Estuary display to 5 May, when trained courier Arun is free. Amend the venue loan end date and book Arun's return train for the next morning, allowing daylight for the unpacking inspection at our store.
Arun confirmed return travel and received unrolling training sign-off. Mina still handles the April outward move.
Home fence posts now set. Test gate swing after hanging the three panels; neighbour asked us to keep the old latch height.

Condition review limits the embroidered hanging to nine weeks of display at the agreed light level. Annotate the survey report with that cap and reduce Bell House's opening by one week so the revised two-venue tour fits within it; send both venues the amended dates.
Bell House countersigned its shortened dates; Estuary's 5 May close remains. Final Stitched journeys itinerary filed with both agreements.
Keep it flat until Monday. No image attached.
Textile baseline photographs complete with colour target, sleeve detail and 20-degree support view. Use these for the next condition comparison.

items.text: Fieldmark first-run sketch: ask walkers to name a place, then write their first trail note. Test whether the blank map before that step is making people quit.
Flowers for Asha's wedding: mixed white stems in low bowls, six tables. Florist needs final table count by the 9th.
'Skip fires twice' on a note beside the laptop. No screen or event name recorded.
Fieldmark analytics draft: onboarding_done fires on leaving the last intro card, first_note_saved only after storage confirms success. Need a separate skipped flag.

Onboarding experiment handoff: variant Cedar removes the blank map and opens the first-note editor immediately. Add intro_variant=Cedar to onboarding_done and first_note_saved, then verify both events after a complete first-run walkthrough. The design test still compares the same task: creating a trail note.
Airplane-mode recording: Fieldmark shows 'saved' for a first trail note, but reopening loses it. Reproduces with a fresh install and no network.
Florist sketch uses tall vases, but Asha asked for low bowls so guests can see across tables. Request corrected proposal.
Cedar first-run test with five volunteers: four reached the editor without help; one looked for an account button. Keep the name-place prompt but explain saving before sign-in.
Event trace on fresh install: onboarding_done emitted twice when app returns from background on the last card. Deduplicate by completed onboarding session, not by screen view.
Offline save diagnosis: first launch creates the local store only after a profile fetch. Initialize the store before any network work so the editor can commit without a profile.
Maybe the local one? recording cuts off immediately.
Wedding table count is seven now, not six. Florist can add one matching low bowl; keep the aisle flowers unchanged.

Measurement correction: onboarding_done must fire on explicit Finish or Skip, not any exit from the last card; backgrounding is neither. Keep first_note_saved tied to the storage confirmation as before.
Offline fix test: three notes survive force-close in airplane mode on a fresh install. Reconnection later uploads each once; the local store initializes without a profile.
Cedar copy change: 'Your note stays on this device until you sign in.' Put this under the first-note editor, above the save button; next test should check what users think happens offline.

Release walkthrough for Fieldmark: with the offline-store fix, first_note_saved arrives only after the local commit even without a connection. Test analytics queue replay on reconnect and assert one saved event for the one surviving note; retain the airplane-mode persistence check in the bug's acceptance notes.

Cedar follow-up: all six participants could explain device-only saving after reading the new sentence. Four created a note; two deliberately skipped. Summarize the comprehension finding alongside the task completion counts.
Florist revised order accepted: seven low bowls, unchanged aisle stems. Cousin Dan will return the bowls on Monday; add his name to the rental pickup sheet.
End of debug log only: 'ok 1 queued 1'. Device and action missing.
Analytics validation complete: Finish and Skip each emit one completion with correct skipped value; returning from background emits none. Saved-note event waits for successful local commit.

items.text: EchoSteps onboarding test: compare microphone permission on launch with asking only when the learner taps Record in lesson one. Prototype label is 'Late mic'.
Pippin needs a walker Tuesday and Thursday while I'm on the early shift. Bea can collect at eight; ask about wet-weather cover.
Spanish onboarding sheet: translator wants screenshots for 'Record', 'Try again' and the sentence explaining microphone access. Text limits differ between buttons and body copy.
First-lesson replay crash recording: finish example audio, tap Replay twice quickly, app closes. Happened after microphone access was denied too.
Experiment report draft: denominator is users who opened lesson one; numerator is users who completed a recording within a day. Break out prompt-on-launch and Late mic cohorts.
Permission prototype interview: learners understood why Record needs the mic, but the launch dialog felt unexplained. Add a one-sentence explanation immediately before the later request.
Pippin walking confirmation: Bea takes Tuesday, Jules Thursday. Spare lead hangs inside the cupboard; both know he shouldn't chase bikes.
Spanish screenshot check: 'Grabar' fits the Record button. The explanatory body sentence wraps to three lines at large text size; allow the panel to grow.
Replay crash stack points to the disposed playback handle. Ignore a second Replay until the first restart has obtained a new handle; cancellation must clear the pending restart.
Rename the 'Late mic' onboarding prototype to 'Ask on Record'. It remains the same request-on-first-record variant; update the review board title and leave the launch-timing control alone.

Report correction: using lesson openers as the denominator drops people put off by the launch permission dialog. Use all newly assigned eligible installs, replacing that draft denominator, and keep completion within a day as numerator.
Pippin soaked the spare lead Tuesday. Put a dry one on the hook before Jules arrives Thursday; Bea's walk itself was fine.
Spanish review of the mic explanation is approved by the translator. Keep 'micrófono' in the body, and use the short verb on the button; export the signed strings sheet.

Ask on Record analysis handoff: freeze the prototype with the explanatory sentence before the permission request, and report outcomes under that final variant name. Rebuild the outcome table from all assigned eligible installs, including those who never reached lesson one; attach the exact screen sequence beside the table so readers know which flow was tested.
Replay fix stress test: ten double-taps after example completion, no crash; leaving the lesson during pending restart cancels cleanly. Repeat once with microphone denied.
Cohort report rebuilt: launch prompt 81/210 completed a recording, Ask on Record 103/214. These are the fixed one-day counts; hold interpretation until checking assignment and missing events.
Ask on Record permission screen at maximum text size: explanation and both actions visible after scrolling. Keep the explicit Not now action in the test build.
Denied-microphone replay check passed: no crash on rapid Replay, and the example audio still works. Close the playback-handle bug.
Spanish onboarding export imported. Screenshots match the signed strings, accents intact, no clipped Record button; translation handoff complete.
'The later one needs checking' — no attachment, subject or quoted message.
